judgements.justification: Neither area chair followed one outlying reviewer: B's meta-review restates all the scores, and A's area chair gave its own reading, which matches 7, 7, 8.
Both committees wrote similar praise but scored it differently: B's generic reviews gave 9 and 8, Reviewer_6QWr's 'very high quality' gave 7, and B's area chair set the oral by the scores alone.
B's reviewers rated above the accept level (a 9 and two 8s), and A also had no dissenting score, so agreement alone did not set B's tier.
Reviewer_9r4w's raise rests on ablations in the paper (Fig. 6), and Reviewer_LgSM's raise names no rebuttal material, so no raise rests on unverified evidence.
B's reviewers named no substantive weakness, and the authors answered their questions, so B's two-sentence 'well-received' meta-review is not a one-sided account.
The two factual errors (Reviewer_yauQ's baseline count, Reviewer_3uQ8's sawyer_push reading) were corrected in the rebuttal, and nothing shows either set a final score.
A's concession that the analysis follows C-learning went to the lower committee, and the C-learning variant result favoured RCE, so no committee ended higher on a damaging admission.
Every objection came before the rebuttal, and no reviewer lowered a score after it.
The scores differ (mean 7.33 against 8.0 with a 9), and A's area chair used its own reading of the paper, so the split is not only a different cut-off.
B's area chair passed over no expert verdict: B's most careful reviewers (Reviewer_9r4w, Reviewer_6QWr) also recommended accept, and A's area chair cited its careful reviewers.

B's concerns (halting, success-example actions, data needs) were questions the response answered, lifting Reviewer_9r4w to 8; A's concerns (simple image tasks, theory from C-learning, unlinked claims) no response could fix, and Reviewer_3uQ8 stayed at 7.
Reviewer_xycR's 9, the outlying champion score from a one-paragraph review, lifted B's mean to 8.0, while B's remaining 8, 7, 8 are close to A's 7, 7, 8.
Reviewer_xycR never engaged after the rebuttal, but the response answered nothing that counted against the 9, so no answered basis stood unrevised.
Neither committee had a detractor; every rating is 7 or higher.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit; A's 'some domains' limits impact, not venue fit.
A's line that reviewers 'initially agreed upon the strong novelty' misfits Reviewer_yauQ, but it points upward and did not set the poster; B's meta-review is accurate.
Non-engagement was similar in both committees (two of three in A, two of four in B never edited), and the one-sided pattern is absent.
B's least confident reviewer, Reviewer_9r4w (math not checked), wrote a specific 8-hour review on empirical points, so the 8 is a checked assessment.
Neither committee split between accept and reject.
The authors answered different questions in each committee but gave no conflicting accounts or numbers; the C-learning concession went to A only because only A asked.
No novelty verdict rests on wrong prior work: Reviewer_yauQ's C-learning claim is correct, and no B reviewer accepted a contradicted 'first' claim.
B's oral matches its scores (8, 9, 7, 8; mean 8.0), and its area chair cited them, so the tier has stated grounds.
No reviewer contested the paper's framing from a neighbouring field.
No reviewer argued for the paper in either visible discussion, and B's top score came from a light review without engagement after the rebuttal.
No committee judged promised revisions too large; both accepted.
Both area chairs worked from the visible reviews; no off-record input appears.
Both committees judged the paper as a method paper by the same standard.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score; every rating is 7 or higher.
